_unit: C5 — judge.me server-HTML opportunistic enrichment (ENABLE_JUDGEME_HTML_REVIEWS, default OFF)
_measurement: M5 measure-judgeme/VERDICT.md — zero-network scan over the 92 cached Gulf PDPs in _proof/html (index _proof/sweep2_curl_cffi.jsonl). 24/24 judge.me hosts by the STRICT multi-marker detector; the 6 bare-'judge' substring pages correctly excluded. Server-side recovery: AGGREGATE RATING for 9/24 (badge or JSON-LD AggregateRating), some REVIEW TEXT for 6/24, 18/24 pure shells. So RATING is PRIMARY, review bodies secondary; this is a small enrichment, not a reviews spine.
_source: read ONLY the merchant's OWN PDP HTML the crawler already holds (its robots governs it) — NEVER judge.me's closed API (B6). No network call at all: the input HTML is parsed in hand.
_hard_rules: STRICT install detector: cdn.judge.me loader OR jdgm.*= config OR jdgm- node class OR id=judgeme_product_reviews. NEVER the bare 'judge' substring (M5: 6/6 false positives — Shopify web pixel webPixelName:'Judge.me', empty integration settings, render-fail app block, minified c.includes('judge'), leftover judgeme-reviews.css asset).
JSON-LD first (AggregateRating + Review[]), then DOM fallback (.jdgm-prev-badge / .jdgm-rev-widg badge + div.jdgm-rev nodes).
Treat a badge of 0.00/0 as ABSENT (client-rendered placeholder), never a real zero.
Drop review bodies of length <= 1 char (albayanperfumes.com's lone body is U+0660 junk).

The measurement's badge 0.00 for myperfumes/parfum was a CSS-SELECTOR false match (.jdgm-prev-badge[data-average-rating='0.00'] inside a <style> block); the parser reads data-average-rating only from a REAL HTML element, so the true DOM badges (myperfumes 4.79/115, parfum 4.15/169) are recovered.

myperfumes_full_jsonld.html.origin: SYNTHETIC — models the measured myperfumes.ae FULL_SERVER page (_proof/html/3933183f7b64d7f046e1ee231c2937112df15441.html). Real page: JSON-LD AggregateRating 4.79/115 + 28 JSON-LD Review objects AND 28 .jdgm-rev__body DOM nodes; DOM prev-badge 4.79/115. Fixture models the SHAPE with 3 JSON-LD reviews (author/rating/date/body) + the agreeing DOM badge. Also carries the CSS 0.00 decoy selector to prove the parser ignores it.
myperfumes_full_jsonld.html.expect: rating source=jsonld 4.79/115; reviews from JSON-LD (3 in fixture) with bodies; JSON-LD wins over DOM.
